name: Autosomal Recessive Hereditary Chronic Pancreatitis

criteria.description: Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in genes associated with hereditary chronic pancreatitis (e.g., PRSS1, SPINK1, CTRC, CFTR)
Recurrent episodes of pancreatitis or chronic pancreatic inflammation documented clinically and biochemically
Imaging findings consistent with chronic pancreatitis such as pancreatic ductal irregularities, calcifications, or atrophy on MRI/MRCP or CT
Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance pattern of chronic pancreatitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of biallelic pathogenic variants plus clinical evidence of recurrent pancreatitis or imaging consistent with chronic pancreatitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm autosomal recessive inheritance; exclusion of other causes of pancreatitis is recommended.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents in childhood or adolescence

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain localized to the epigastrium

searchTerms: weight loss from poor nutrient absorption

common.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to pancreatic endocrine insufficiency
searchTerms: diabetes caused by pancreas hormone failure
high blood sugar from pancreas problems
secondary diabetes due to pancreas damage

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting during acute episodes
searchTerms: feeling sick with vomiting during attacks

occasional.symptomName: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K
jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile
bone weakness from pancreas enzyme deficiency
bone loss due to enzyme shortage

laboratory: Elevated serum amylase and lipase during acute episodes
Fecal elastase deficiency indicating exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
Abnormal glucose tolerance tests indicating endocrine insufficiency
imaging: Pancreatic ductal irregularities and dilatation on MRCP or ERCP
Pancreatic calcifications visible on CT scan
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in PRSS1, SPINK1, CTRC, or CFTR genes confirming autosomal recessive hereditary pancreatitis
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Histopathology showing chronic inflammation and fibrosis of pancreatic tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Typically caused by heterozygous PRSS1 mutations
Earlier onset and more severe disease course
Presence of CFTR mutations associated with cystic fibrosis

redFlags: Rapid progression to pancreatic exocrine and endocrine insufficiency
Development of pancreatic ductal strictures or obstruction
Family history of early-onset pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer
references: Witt H, Apte MV, Keim V, Wilson JS. Chronic pancreatitis: challenges and advances in pathogenesis, genetics, diagnosis, and therapy. Gastroenterology. 2007;132(4):1557-1573.
